crossRefs.note: ‘Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, utter a song! Arise, Barak, and lead away your captives, you son of Abinoam.’
Awake, awake! Put on your strength, Zion. Put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city: for from now on the…
Break out into joy! Sing together, you waste places of Jerusalem; for Yahweh has comforted his people. He has redeemed…
Therefore my heart is glad, and my tongue rejoices. My body shall also dwell in safety.
to the end that my heart may sing praise to you, and not be silent. Yahweh my God, I will give thanks to you forever!
My heart is steadfast, God. I will sing and I will make music with my soul.
Therefore my heart was glad, and my tongue rejoiced. Moreover my flesh also will dwell in hope;

translations.web: Wake up, my glory! Wake up, lute and harp! I will wake up the dawn.
translations.bsb: Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn.
translations.kjv: Awake up, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp: I myself will awake early.
translations.asv: Awake up, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp: I myself will awake right early.
